This occurred within a broader context of an aggressive U.S. pressure campaign that intensified throughout the latter half of the year.

grounding_supports.segment_text: On November 6, 2025, the U.S. Senate voted down a proposed War Powers Resolution that would have limited the president's ability to take military action.
This vote happened as the Trump administration was signaling that its anti-drug campaign in the region could involve military force inside Venezuela.

A significant event during this week was a Spanish raid on November 8, 2025, which led to the arrest of thirteen individuals across multiple cities suspected of being members of the Venezuelan Tren de Aragua crime group.
This action was notable as the Trump administration had recently designated the gang as a terrorist organization.
The period from September to November 2025 was marked by a peak in tensions, with Washington launching a maritime "anti-narcotics" campaign in the Caribbean and Pacific.
This campaign involved numerous strikes against alleged drug smuggling boats.
Ford aircraft carrier group, for an operation dubbed "Southern Spear".
The Federal Aviation Administration also issued a warning to airlines about potential dangers in Venezuelan airspace due to increased military activity.
A phone call reportedly took place on November 21 between President Trump and Nicolás Maduro, in which Trump allegedly gave Maduro a one-week deadline to resign.
By December, a Brazilian official was warning that the U.S. closure of Venezuelan airspace was an "act of war" that could plunge the region into a Vietnam-style conflict.
This period of heightened confrontation culminated in a U.S. military operation in January 2026 that resulted in the capture of President Nicolás Maduro.
